 EXCLUSIVE: Today, Saturday Night Live alumni Bobby Moynihan , Aristotle Athari and Taran Killam launched On Display , a new podcast birthed out of their shared passion for collectibles.
 The trio loves collecting everything from comic books to action figures and movie memorabilia. Each week on the podcast, they’ll be joined by a celebrity guest to talk about their cherished items and hobbies, while sharing their own personal fandoms. The show brings together comedy, nostalgia and often-heartfelt stories about personal obsessions, and what certain prized possessions really mean to both the hosts and their guests.

 On Display premiered today at 9 a.m. PT. New episodes will go out weekly on Mondays across YouTube and wherever else podcasts are found. The first season will feature 12 episodes, with five or six already shot. Watch a special preview above and the full first episode below.
 Watch on Deadline 
 The pod is produced by StudioTen42 , in association with the comedian-owned podcast network All Things Comedy . Billy Rosenberg and Drew Eller are exec producing for ATC, alongside Guy Robinson for StudioTen42, and Andy Smith for high-end collectibles company, Sideshow , which is the show’s sponsor.
 Athari came to the idea for On Display after connecting with Andy Smith, who works in PR at Sideshow, during his time working on the film M3GAN 2.0 . Through Smith, he learned that Killam is a passionate collector who lost a collection he’d spent decades building — featuring some irreplaceable items — when his house burned down in the devastating Palisades Fire of January 2025. On Saturday Night Live for just one season, from 2021-2022, Athari hadn’t overlapped there with either Moynihan, who did nine seasons from 2008-2017, or Killam, who was on for six seasons from 2010-2016. After learning about what had happened to Killam, he began working with Sideshow to help him rebuild his collection. Then, he leaned that Moynihan is an avid collector, as well, leading to initial discussions amongst the trio about On Display .
 Killam told Deadline, “Hosting this podcast is beyond fun. Being a collector my entire life has directly informed what I do for a living. It’s been great interviewing other accomplished collectors and learning how it informs their own professional process. It’s also really great to see lots of really cool toys.”
 Moynihan commented, “I love talking about things I love with people I love while people who love things watch this thing we hope they love because we also love…it.”
 Athari added, for his part, “I feel immensely fortunate to share my affinity for collecting ephemera with friends and transform that shared passion into a creative and entertaining endeavor. Apparently, the only difference between collecting and hoarding is having a podcast.”
 Moynihan is repped by UTA, OPE Partners and Jackoway Austen Tyerman; Athari by CAA, Stride Management and Gang, Tyre Ramer; and Killam by UTA and Ziffren Brittenham.
